chunks: And Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi narrated from Muhammad ibn Ibad al-Muhallabi who said:

When Harun al-Rashid imprisoned Abu Ibrahim Musa (peace be upon him) and he displayed signs and miracles while in prison, al-Rashid was bewildered. He summoned Yahya ibn Khalid al-Barmaki and said to him: 'O Abu Ali, do you not see what we are in from these wonders? Do you not consider the affair of this man with a plan that relieves us from his worry?' So Yahya ibn Khalid al-Barmaki said to him: 'What I advise you to do, O Commander of the Faithful, is to show him favor and connect his kinship, for by Allah, he has spoiled the hearts of our followers against us.' And Yahya was favoring him, while Harun did not know that. So Harun said: 'Go to him, release the iron from him, and convey my greetings to him, and say to him: Your cousin says: An oath has preceded from me concerning you that I will not release you until you admit to me the mistreatment, and ask me for forgiveness for what has passed from you. And there is no disgrace upon you in your admission, nor any deficiency in your asking me. And this is Yahya ibn Khalid (he is) my trustworthy one, my minister, and the manager of my affairs. So ask him to the extent that he removes me from my oath, and he will depart successfully.'

key_terms.أبو إبراهيم موسى عليه السلام: Abu Ibrahim Musa (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Musa al-Kadim
key_terms.البرقي: Al-Barqi, a narrator known for his work 'Al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil'
key_terms.الدلائل: Signs/Proofs, referring to miraculous evidence of his status
key_terms.يحيى بن خالد البرمكي: Yahya ibn Khalid al-Barmaki, a prominent vizier

ai.seo_question: How did Harun al-Rashid plan to release Imam Musa al-Kadhim while maintaining his political standing?
ai.summary: This account from Al-Tabari and Al-Tusi highlights the political maneuvering of the Abbasid court, where Caliph Harun al-Rashid, baffled by Imam Musa al-Kadim's (AS) miracles, sought Yahya ibn Khalid al-Barmaqi's counsel. Yahya, secretly favoring the Imam, advised a diplomatic release by leveraging Harun's oath, allowing the Imam to concede to mistreatment to preserve the Caliph's dignity. This narrative underscores the interplay between divine signs and political pragmatism in the Imam's life, illustrating how the Ahl al-Bayt navigated Abbasid authority with wisdom and grace.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 4 - Muhammad bin Khalid Barqi has narrated from Muhammad bin Ibad Muhallabi that

when Harun Rashid imprisoned Imam Kadhim (a.s) and His Eminence also displayed miracles in the prison itself in order to prove his rightfulness, Harun Rashid was bewildered; till he summoned Yahya bin Khalid Barmaki and said: “O Abu Ali, do you not see the wonders in which we are? Do you not consider the affair of this man (Imam Musa) and relieve us from his worry?” So he advised correctly and guided him to a good deed, saying to him: “Commander of the faithful, I think that you have to be kind to him and to link to his womb relatives. For, by Allah, he has spoiled the hearts of our followers against us.” Harun Rashid responded to his advice, saying to him: “Go to him, remove the iron from him, give him my regards, and say: ‘Your cousin says: I have sworn by Allah concerning you that I will not release you unless you admit that you have mistreated me. You must ask me to forgive your past deeds. There is no disgrace in your admitting (that), nor is there any defect in your asking me for that. This is Yahya bin Khalid, my trustworthy one, minister and head of my affairs. So ask him in as much as I get rid of my oath and you would also be able to return to Medina safely.”’
